summary: New sense 2: (mit ʕal-) über jemanden beten
rationale: PrS 53/14 and 53/34 repeatedly put Malke as praying agent over another person, unlike confessant-subject sense 1. PrS 34/113 supplies a matching priest-over-head rite before baptism; its precise liturgical interpretation is unresolved.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 34/113)

data.turoyo: Maṣlawle lu qašo ʕar riša w mʕamḏole. Mhəlle a tləṯ aʕle.
data.translation: Der Pfaffe liess sie nun beichten und taufte sie, dann traute er ihm die drei Frauen an.

rationale: First evidence for ritual-agent plus ʕal-head construction; edition's liess sie beichten retained without inventing absolution.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 53/14)

data.turoyo: Mawfaqle u šiḏo me gawa, msəkle. Maṣlawle ʕar riša, nayəḥla.
data.translation: Er hiess den Teufel aus ihrem Leibe herausgehen und nahm ihn gefangen, dann betete er über ihr, und sie war geheilt.

rationale: New construction with explicit over-her-head target and recovery, separate from confessant-subject beichten.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 53/34)

summary: III.1 has the confessing person as subject and can specify the confessor with gabe. New III.2 has priest/Malke as agent and another person or their head as ʕal-target; this participant contrast supports a construction sense.

Lookup ṣly II confirms mṣalele ʕal riši at 40/30 with the same prayer-over-person construction. The supplied maṣlaw- spelling matches this entry's III base; retain its provisional filing without asserting a lexical or historical split.
PrS 34/113 precedes baptism, 53/14 follows exorcism and 53/34 concerns the fallen. These contextual rites do not establish three separate lexical senses or prove sacramental absolution.

Legacy prs 175/22 and prs 226/24 appear to locate the same passages now supplied as PrS 62/90 and PrS 77/60. Preserve inherited references; text/verse equivalents are recorded here rather than replacing potentially valid page/line locators.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; quoted English is copied from the supplied machine translation.
The following məṣṭaʕrafle denotes confession with the convert as subject, while Maṣlawlan has plural praying agents and a ʕal-head target. This corroborates the distinction already made in round 1.
maṣlawwo is in a repeated-past wedding account, contrasting with overt L-series Maṣlawlan. Infectum-wa is the provisional filing; it must not be reinterpreted from English tense alone.

Permitted lookup of ṣly II confirms mṣalele ʕal riši prayer over a person. Formal maṣlaw- resemblance motivates keeping the present tokens under the assigned ṣlw2 III entry provisionally; no consolidation or historical stem claim is made.
Are maṣlawle/maṣalwi/maṣluwi variant forms of ṣly II mṣalele/mṣale or a distinct III paradigm? Compare ṣly II 40/30 before consolidating entries.
PrS 34/113: identify the rite precisely: hearing confession, absolution, preparatory prayer, or another act over the head. Proposed sense 2 keeps the broader prayer construction supported by PrS 53.
Verify legacy page/line to text/verse mappings prs 175/22 ↔ PrS 62/90 and prs 226/24 ↔ PrS 77/60 before editing inherited citation formats.
Confirm maṣlawwo pronunciation and paradigm: ṣlw2 III variant, ṣly II variant, or transcription error? If ṣly II, relocate the token rather than adding a new sense there.
Does praying over wedding bread entail blessing, or only reciting prayer? The proposal deliberately preserves broad prayer wording.
Confirm the plural agents and target of Maṣlawlan in3.33/910; do not collapse this action into the convert's following confession.
Female bears confess in a fable; ordinary confessant-subject meaning and gabe confessor frame are retained.

Jan supports round-1 prayer-over-target2. Bread extends the target beyond persons; reception of a convert repeats the head construction. Neither proves blessing or sacramental absolution as a separate lexical meaning.
